A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DS-CP work. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original CP-versus-DS-CP coverage and prediction-set analyses across 272 MMLU subject pairs and 16 LLMs, including APS results in Appendix B. Reusing existing model logits does not remove the originality of these analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports the corresponding MMLU analyses, revised results, and additional regularization, embedding-model and classifier ablations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 change the default regularizer from λ=1 to λ=max_i w_i, affecting the conformal threshold within the existing framework. Embedding, density-ratio estimation and weighted quantiles remain; explicit target-batch inputs and shared-threshold outputs clarify the previously described workflow.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same processed MMLU multiple-choice data: 17 subjects and 272 ordered calibration–test subject pairs. The added component ablations retain this coverage; temporal, stylistic and open-ended-generation scenarios remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: Standard CP remains the only external conformal comparator actually evaluated in the LAC and APS experiments. Weighted and nonexchangeable CP receive discussion but no new comparative results; alternative embeddings and classifiers are DS-CP component ablations.

E3.justification: V2 explicitly specifies λ=max_i w_i throughout the experiments, replacing v1's default λ=1 recommendation. It adds controlled regularization and component sweeps and a calibration-and-test bootstrap check. The underlying data, preprocessing, 16 LLMs, 90% target coverage and coverage/set-size metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained APS and paired-coverage analyses, Appendix B adds a six-value regularization sweep across all models and controlled embedding and classifier sensitivity studies on four LLMs. Figures 5–10 examine MiniLM/MPNet/E5 and XGBoost/MLP/logistic regression, substantially expanding evidence about which components drive coverage and efficiency.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports bootstrapping both calibration and test instances with replacement and qualitatively compares bootstrap means and medians with full-data coverage. It supplies no replicate count or confidence intervals. The fixed classifier seed is retained, and ablation minima/medians/maxima describe variation across subject pairs rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: The LAC distributions in Figures 1–3 and APS distributions, matched from v1 Figures 5–7 to v2 Figures 11–13, change alongside the revised regularizer; updated set-size histograms include full six-answer sets. New Figures 5–10 report the coverage-versus-size regularization tradeoff and broadly similar behavior across alternative components. These are revised and additional results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces unconditional total-variation bounds multiplied by weight suprema with expectations involving total variation conditional on the learned weights. It revises the independence assumptions and lower-bound proof, adds embedding-space score-smoothness bounds and an effective-sample-size proposition, and develops their proofs in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract and central coverage/efficiency contributions largely remain. However, v2's introduction and Discussion qualify adaptation as domain-level recalibration using a shared target-batch threshold and describe novelty more specifically as the combination of semantic embeddings, density-ratio weighting and regularized conformal prediction.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations based on conditional score smoothness and effective sample size. Its rewritten Discussion explicitly identifies the unlabeled target-batch requirement, transductive evaluation, limited baseline comparisons and the distinction between larger prediction sets and intrinsic LLM reliability. These materially sharpen applicability and failure conditions beyond v1's limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link and documents computing and reusing one threshold after offline target-batch adaptation. Appendix C retains the same data/logit source, excluded indices, XGBoost hyperparameters, seed and hardware. Comparable implementation details for the newly tested alternative components remain limited.

R1.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands comparisons with existing LLM conformal methods, including new citations to Ren et al., Cherian et al. and Wang et al.'s ConU. It explicitly positions DS-CP against exchangeability-dependent methods, heuristic similarity weighting and approaches requiring specified shift mechanisms. Publication-metadata updates to existing references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the coverage exposition and Discussion, recasts Algorithm 1, and introduces a dedicated related-work section. It also standardizes source/target terminology, compacts notation and reorganizes explanations around regularizer selection and structured appendix ablations.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, with formerly full-page figures reduced and embedded beside text. Six ablation figures are added, and retained APS displays are relocated and renumbered from Figures 5–7 to Figures 11–13. This substantially changes visual organization and figure legibility.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important theory–practice mismatch: v1 recommends λ=1 although its bounds require λ≥max_i w_i, while v2's default satisfies that condition. The weight-conditioned coverage analysis, supporting ablations and explicit batch/transductive limitations substantially strengthen rigor and interpretability. These gains outweigh reduced figure legibility, although comparative baseline breadth and bootstrap documentation remain limited.
